events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.88)
events.body:
The dispute is a cancellation-fee (no-show) case: the driver cancelled the RydeX trip at 22:45:05, 8 min 5 s after acceptance, and $6.61 was charged to the rider [F4][F7]. NS-0 routes a driver-cancellation-with-no-show-allegation case into NS-1/NS-2 [F4][NS-0].

NS-1 makes the fee conditional on the cumulative satisfaction of (i) the driver pressing "I'm Here", (ii) GPS placing the driver at the pickup point at that moment, and (iii) more than 3 minutes of waiting there. The system timeline records that the driver never tapped "I'm Here" (driver_pressed_here_at is null) [F6], and the driver's own statement confirms it — "I forgot to press the I'm Here button" [F11]. Because a system record governs over a party statement where they conflict, and here both agree, element NS-1(i) is not met [F6][F11][NS-1].

The driver's advocate argues the GPS record substitutes for the missing tap: closest approach 33 m at 22:41:00, stationary 38 m from the pickup 22:41:05–22:45:05, cumulative 5 min 20 s within 200 m [F1][F2][F3][F5]. Those facts satisfy the substance of (ii) and (iii), but NS-1 is written as a conjunctive test — NS-2 expressly provides that the fee does not stand if any one of (i)(ii)(iii) is not fulfilled — so the missing precondition is fatal regardless of the GPS showing [F1][F3][F6][NS-1][NS-2]. The rider's admitted "on my way down" status is only a party statement with no system record of her position, and it does not restore the fee once (i) fails [NS-1][NS-2].

NS-2 therefore applies: the $6.61 cancellation fee must be refunded in full, and the amount equals the fee on record, [F7], with no surge so no adjustment applies [F8][NS-2][NS-7]. The aggravated limb of NS-2 (flag_account for tapping "I'm Here" while away from the pickup) is not triggered — no tap was ever made [F6].

I do not reach RD-1/RD-2 detour analysis: the fare model is a fixed quotation for RydeX and no off-route segment facts exist in this file [F7][RD-2][FARE-1]. Traffic and weather facts (speed band 3, no incidents, fair weather) are unremarkable and do not bear on NS-1's elements [F12][F13][F14].

Per NS-7 the refund is issued as a Ryde voucher, not cash [NS-7].

ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher per NS-7; note on the driver's record that the trip was cancelled without the required "I'm Here" arrival confirmation (NS-1(i)), and remind the driver that arrival and waiting-fee conditions must be evidenced by the in-app button.

events.body:
RIDER: We reviewed your cancellation fee dispute and you're getting the $6.61 back in full, issued as a Ryde voucher rather than cash.

The deciding fact: the fee can only be charged if the driver tapped "I'm Here" in the app during the wait at your pickup point, and no such tap was recorded — the driver also confirmed it wasn't made. So the fee didn't stand, and the amount refunded matches the fee you were charged.

Nothing else is needed from you. The voucher will be applied to your account for use on your next trips.

DRIVER: We reviewed the cancellation fee on this trip. The fee has been refunded to the rider in full as a Ryde voucher, and no fee will be paid to you.

The deciding fact: the fee requires you to tap "I'm Here" in the app at the pickup point before the wait can count, and no such tap was recorded on this trip — you also confirmed it wasn't made. Your location history during the wait didn't change the outcome, because the tap is required.

This will be noted on your record, and we're asking you to press "I'm Here" every time you reach the pickup point so arrival and waiting time are properly evidenced. No other action is needed from you right now.

ruling.reasoning:
The dispute is a cancellation-fee (no-show) case: the driver cancelled the RydeX trip at 22:45:05, 8 min 5 s after acceptance, and $6.61 was charged to the rider [F4][F7]. NS-0 routes a driver-cancellation-with-no-show-allegation case into NS-1/NS-2 [F4][NS-0].

NS-1 makes the fee conditional on the cumulative satisfaction of (i) the driver pressing "I'm Here", (ii) GPS placing the driver at the pickup point at that moment, and (iii) more than 3 minutes of waiting there. The system timeline records that the driver never tapped "I'm Here" (driver_pressed_here_at is null) [F6], and the driver's own statement confirms it — "I forgot to press the I'm Here button" [F11]. Because a system record governs over a party statement where they conflict, and here both agree, element NS-1(i) is not met [F6][F11][NS-1].

The driver's advocate argues the GPS record substitutes for the missing tap: closest approach 33 m at 22:41:00, stationary 38 m from the pickup 22:41:05–22:45:05, cumulative 5 min 20 s within 200 m [F1][F2][F3][F5]. Those facts satisfy the substance of (ii) and (iii), but NS-1 is written as a conjunctive test — NS-2 expressly provides that the fee does not stand if any one of (i)(ii)(iii) is not fulfilled — so the missing precondition is fatal regardless of the GPS showing [F1][F3][F6][NS-1][NS-2]. The rider's admitted "on my way down" status is only a party statement with no system record of her position, and it does not restore the fee once (i) fails [NS-1][NS-2].

NS-2 therefore applies: the $6.61 cancellation fee must be refunded in full, and the amount equals the fee on record, [F7], with no surge so no adjustment applies [F8][NS-2][NS-7]. The aggravated limb of NS-2 (flag_account for tapping "I'm Here" while away from the pickup) is not triggered — no tap was ever made [F6].

I do not reach RD-1/RD-2 detour analysis: the fare model is a fixed quotation for RydeX and no off-route segment facts exist in this file [F7][RD-2][FARE-1]. Traffic and weather facts (speed band 3, no incidents, fair weather) are unremarkable and do not bear on NS-1's elements [F12][F13][F14].

Per NS-7 the refund is issued as a Ryde voucher, not cash [NS-7].

claims.assertion: The driver cancelled this trip and a $6.61 cancellation fee was charged to the rider, so the fee's validity is governed by NS-1/NS-2.
NS-1(i) fails: the system timeline shows the driver never pressed "I'm Here" (driver_pressed_here_at is null), and the driver's own chat statement admits "I forgot to press the I'm Here button".
Because the mandatory "I'm Here" condition of NS-1 is unmet, NS-2 applies and the $6.61 cancellation fee must be refunded in full to the rider.
The rider's account history (719 days, rating 4.5, zero disputes and zero upheld claims in 90 days) shows no pattern of no-shows supporting the fee.
The refund amount is fixed by the fare record: the cancellation fee actually charged is $6.61 and no surge applies, so $6.61 is the full sum to be returned.

NS-2's aggravated limb (false arrival claim triggering flag_account) is not pressed against the driver: he never tapped "I'm Here", so there is no false arrival-button use by him; the rider's claim rests on the missing tap alone.

weaknesses: The driver did in fact reach and wait near the pickup point: GPS puts him 33 m away at 22:41:00 (F1), stationary 38 m away for 4 min 0 s from 22:41:05 to 22:45:05 (F3), and within 200 m for a cumulative 5 min 20 s (F2/F5) — i.e. the substantive NS-1 (ii)(iii) facts favour the driver, and only the procedural "I'm Here" tap (F6) is missing.

The rider's own complaint admits "I was on my way down", so the other side will argue the rider was not at the pickup point during the 4-minute wait, making the delay the rider's and the driver's tap omission merely clerical.
The driver's written statement (F11) and chat messages (F9, F10) present a coherent "waited 4 min then cancelled" account that a judge may read as good faith rather than as a fee-triggering abuse.

If the judge treated the missing tap as a technicality outweighed by the GPS arrival record (F2, F5), the outcome would flip to no_action and the $6.61 would stand; the rider's case rests on the policy making the tap a strict precondition.

claims.assertion: The driver was physically at the pickup point: GPS puts his closest approach at 33 m at 22:41:00 and he was stationary 38 m from the pickup from 22:41:05 to the cancellation at 22:45:05, well inside the 200 m arrival radius.

The driver waited at the pickup point longer than the 3-minute threshold: he was within 200 m from 22:39:45 and stayed there until cancelling at 22:45:05, a cumulative 5 min 20 s inside the radius (4 min 0 s stationary), so NS-1(iii)'s '> 3 minutes' requirement is met on the system record.

The rider's own account is consistent with a no-show: she says she was still 'on my way down' at cancellation time, i.e. she had not reached the pickup point after the driver had been waiting there for over five minutes.

The only unmet NS-1 element is the button press — the driver never tapped 'I'm Here' (F6) and admits this in his statement — but the GPS record independently establishes the substantive facts the button is meant to evidence (presence at the pickup point and 3+ minutes of waiting), so the $6.61 rider cancellation fee should stand as correctly levied.
The fee amount is the published $6.61 with no surge (multiplier 1.0x), so no part of the charge is an unpublished or inflated add-on.
Neither party has any dispute history in the last 90 days (rider 0, driver 0 upheld), so there is no basis for a flag_account action against the driver in this case.

Traffic and weather during the trip window were unremarkable (no incidents near the route, fair weather, speed band 3 at 20-29 km/h), so nothing external prevented the rider from reaching the pickup point within the wait.

weaknesses: The driver never tapped 'I'm Here' (F6); under a literal reading of NS-1 element (i) and NS-2, the rider will argue the $6.61 must be refunded in full solely because the threshold act was not performed — the policy requires all three of (i)(ii)(iii).

The driver's own written statement admits the omission ('I forgot to press the I'm Here button'), which the rider will quote (F11); chat/statements lose to system records, but here the system record F6 agrees with the admission, so it cannot be argued away.

The rider's claim that she was 'on my way down' is only her statement; no system fact shows her position, so the no-show conclusion rests on the absence of any rider-side GPS rather than positive proof she failed to arrive.

points.response: Not contested as fact: GPS shows the driver 33 m away at 22:41:00 and stationary 38 m away from 22:41:05 (F1, F3), but NS-1 requires (i), (ii) and (iii) to be satisfied cumulatively, and presence alone cannot satisfy element (i).

The waiting duration is not disputed (5 min 20 s inside 200 m, F2/F5), but NS-1(iii) is only reached after NS-1(i) and (ii) are met, and the policy states that if any of (i)(ii)(iii) is not fulfilled the fee does not stand.

The rider's phrase 'on my way down' is only a party statement, and no system fact records her position; what the system does record is that the arrival button was never pressed (F6), which is the contractual condition the driver had to satisfy.

This is the crux and it fails: NS-1 (i) is an express precondition ('Driver has pressed I'm Here'), the unchallenged system record shows driver_pressed_here_at is null (F6), and the driver admits the omission (F11) — so NS-2 applies on its face and the fee must be refunded in full, not the GPS substituted for the required act.
The amount being the published $6.61 (F7, F8) is beside the point: whether the fee is chargeable at all is governed by NS-1/NS-2, and the condition precedent in NS-1(i) was not performed (F6).
Conceded: with zero upheld disputes on both sides (F15, F16) there is no basis under NS-2 for a flag_account action, and the rider does not seek one — only the $6.61 refund.
Agreed and immaterial: no incident was recorded near the route and weather was fair (F12, F13, F14), so this case turns solely on the unmet NS-1(i) arrival-button condition (F6).

Conceded as framed: the fee's validity is governed by NS-1/NS-2 because the driver cancelled (F4) and $6.61 was charged (F7), but that framing does not decide the case — NS-1's substantive elements (ii) and (iii) are fully satisfied on the system record.

We do not contest that the tap is absent (F6, F11); what the rider cannot show is any system fact contradicting the driver's presence — GPS places him 33 m from the pickup at 22:41:00 and stationary at 38 m for 4 min 0 s until the cancellation (F1, F3).

NS-2 is not triggered merely by a missing tap in the abstract; the tap evidences the two conditions it exists to prove, and here those conditions are directly established by GPS: within 200 m from 22:39:45 for a cumulative 5 min 20 s (F2, F5) and stationary 4 min 0 s at the pickup point (F3), i.e. presence plus a wait exceeding 3 minutes, exactly as NS-1(ii)(iii) require.

The rider's clean record (F15) says nothing about this trip; the operative fact is that at cancellation the rider was still 'on my way down', i.e. not at the pickup point after the driver had been waiting there over five minutes (F2, F5).

The $6.61 figure is not in dispute (F7, no surge per F8) — what is in dispute is whether it is refundable at all, and on the GPS record the charge reflects a genuine rider no-show, so there is no sum to return.

We accept no false arrival-button use occurred (F6), and equally no flag_account action is warranted against the driver: he has 1059 days on the platform, 770 trips in 90 days, 0 disputes and 0 upheld (F16), and there was no incident or adverse condition excusing the rider's absence (F12, F13, F14).
